subject: Contract redline: carveout for inference telemetry audit window — request for Product & Security sign-off
messages:
From: Janelle Park <janelle.park@acmehealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Security Team <sec-requests@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Acme DPA redline (telemetry audit window)

Stephanie — attaching our redline to the DPA. Two asks related to inference telemetry:

1) We need a 36-month retention window for audit logs from any runtime that processes PHI/PII.
2) We want the right to conduct an annual subprocessor audit and require subprocessor names for any analytics vendor that receives inference telemetry.

Both items are highlighted in the attached PDF (Acme-DPA_redline_v3.pdf). Let me know if Redwood can accept these or propose carveouts. Acme would prefer to limit any carveout to non-identifiable telemetry only.

Thanks,
Janelle
Senior Counsel, Acme Health
[Attachment: Acme-DPA_redline_v3.pdf (pdf)]

Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Acme DPA redline (telemetry audit window) — need Product/Sec/Legal guidance

Folks — forwarding Acme's redline. Key asks: 36-month audit log retention and the right to audit analytics subprocessors.

Context: Acme is a potential Dedicated customer with PHI scope; Product and Security need to confirm operational impact and whether we can offer a carveout scoped to "non-identifying telemetry". Legal (Laura) — please advise on contractual language if we offer a partial acceptance (e.g., limit to aggregated KV cache metrics, not raw prompts/outputs).

Ask: Can Product & Security provide a proposed response and acceptance matrix by EOD Friday so I can send to Acme next week? I'm attaching a short proposal I drafted with two carveout options.

[Attachment: inference-telemetry-exception-proposal.docx]

Thanks — S.

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Acme DPA redline (telemetry audit window) — initial Sec review

Thanks for the heads up. Quick notes from Security after a preliminary review: 

- 36 months for audit logs is longer than our standard 12–24 month retention for telemetry; operational cost and cross-customer isolation need evaluation.
- We must be explicit about what constitutes "inference telemetry". If Acme expects raw prompts/outputs or model input traces to be retained for 36 months, we need to push back.
- Subprocessor audit: we can provide a subprocessor list and commit to an annual attestation from analytics vendors, but we do not normally allow customer-led audits of third-party vendors unless under a special enterprise SOC arrangement.

Questions for Product: what telemetry do we currently persist for Dedicated customers' inference paths? (KV cache metadata? token-level latency traces? raw request/response records?) Also need cost estimate to extend retention to 36 months (S3 + warm storage + searchability).

I'll draft suggested language that limits retention and allows a SOC-style attestation in lieu of direct audits.

—Olga
Olga Petrov
Head of Product Security
Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, olga_petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Jun 2027 11:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Acme DPA redline (telemetry audit window) — Product impact and options

Stephanie/Team — Product notes and tradeoffs: 

1) Current default telemetry for Dedicated runtime: aggregated token metrics, latency histograms, error rates, and anonymized sampling of request identifiers. We do not retain raw prompt/response pairs except for short retention windows used for debugging (configurable per-customer, default 7 days).

2) To meet a 36-month retention for audit logs we can propose two options:
  a) "Aggregated Audit Window" — retain only aggregated metrics and event-level metadata (no payloads) for 36 months. Low overhead, aligns with our privacy posture.
  b) "Full Audit (by exception)" — retain raw request/response for customers who sign a premium addendum and accept storage/cost implications. This requires legal approval, procurement of dedicated encryption key rotation procedures, and an internal Ops runbook.

3) Subprocessor audits: Product is aligned with Security that we can provide a named subprocessor list and quarterly attestations from analytics vendors. Customer-conducted audits would require a SOC/Marketplace offering or an on-site audit playbook (high friction).

Recommendation: Offer option (a) by default and (b) as a paid enterprise add-on with strict controls. Laura — if Legal can draft language that accepts aggregated retention for 36 months and keeps raw payload retention to "by exception only" we should be able to close.

Dev Patel
Principal Product Manager, Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, olga_petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 16:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Acme DPA redline (telemetry audit window) — proposed response

Team — drafting language now. Proposed approach to send to Acme: 

1) Acceptance in principle of a 36-month audit retention for aggregated telemetry (latency histograms, counts, anonymized event metadata) only.
2) Explicit carveout: raw prompts, model outputs, and any request payloads will not be retained longer than a customer-configurable debug window (default 7 days) unless an additional written addendum is signed ("Full Audit Addendum").
3) Subprocessor transparency: Redwood will provide a current subprocessor list and quarterly attestations from analytics subprocessors. For customers requiring direct audits, Redwood will offer a SOC-based review or a vendor-led attestation process; direct customer audits of third parties will not be granted as a standard right.

I will prepare two short paragraphs for Stephanie to respond with: one that accepts Acme's concern over auditability and proposes the aggregated retention carveout, and one that describes the enterprise add-on path.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Contracts
Redwood Inference
